form: A small, steep-gabled two-storey brick house (the family villa's shape redrawn in the dream's Art Nouveau language) standing alone in an open earth-and-grass clearing at the edge of the wood, front door facing the wood; a tall kitchen chimney stack pours pepper-smoke. Exterior only
culture_ref: geography.json#LOC-duchess-house; world.json#wonderland_real_counterparts cp-cat; SCN-riverbank architecture (family villa: gabled polychrome-brick Gothic Revival); culture.json CUL-008, CUL-012
period: Dream-image of an 1860s north-Oxford villa, reduced to its service end (brick, a kitchen chimney and a door for tradesmen and staff), its trim redrawn in the dream's licensed Art Nouveau (WR-010); props and costumes stay 1862

grows_from.waking_detail: the family house's service door, where below-stairs life a child knows only at second hand spills out
grows_from.design_growth: The family villa's service wing detached and set down alone in the wood: same polychrome brick banding, same steep slate roof as the villa glimpsed from the bank, its door-head now a flowing horseshoe arch, but squeezed into a narrow two-bay house whose only face is its tradesmen's door. The noise and smoke of the kitchen, which a child upstairs only hears, are here the whole building

dream_design_language: Familiar villa vocabulary made cramped and slightly wrong: the gable too steep, the front door too tall for the facade, the chimney too big for the house; windows smoked grey from inside so the house looks blind. The Art Nouveau ornament is there but sooted and neglected, gold showing through grime

mucha_design_language.item: Mucha / Art Nouveau on a small service house: a flowing horseshoe-arched door surround of carved Bath stone with lily-and-vine relief; a round stained-glass halo roundel in the gable (glass smoked grey-amber from inside); a mosaic frieze band of pastel and gold tesserae under the eaves, cracked and sooted; wrought-iron whiplash brackets on the gutter and a whiplash-scroll boot-scraper; pastel-and-gold showing through soot
mucha_design_language.why: Dream environments carry the language fully; soot keeps the house's grim, noisy character

structure.item: free-standing house in an open place, two bays wide, gable end facing the clearing, ridge about 7.2 m at hero scale (see scale_notes)
structure.note: 'a little house in it about four feet high'; form, bays and height ratio inferred from the family villa, culture_ref SCN-riverbank architecture structure (villa)

structure.item: one front door, the only entrance, reached by a single worn stone step; the Frog-Footman (CGI frog-bodied figure in livery) sits on the ground beside it
a tall square brick chimney stack on the rear gable with grey smoke rolling from it
structure.why: The kitchen's smoke must be readable from the doorstep scenes

structure.item: two small ground-floor windows either side of the door and one upper window in the gable (a round halo roundel), all with small leaded panes smoked grey from inside
structure.why: Gives the kitchen noise a visible source without showing the interior

structure.item: open place in front: an irregular clearing about 14 m across of trodden earth and patchy grass, the wood closing in on three sides; Alice hides and peeps from the tree line opposite the door
a path of beaten earth running from the clearing into the wood on the far side (the way the pig trots off, and on to the Cheshire Cat's path)

materials.item: soft red hand-made brick with two bands of dark blue-black brick (the waking villa's polychrome brick)
materials.why: Carries the waking villa's material into the dream so the grows_from link is visible

materials.item: Bath-stone dressings carved in flowing Art Nouveau relief: horseshoe door arch with lily-and-vine carving, window sills and kneelers, sooted grey
materials.why: The villa's trim redrawn in the dream's language; soot ties it to the smoke

materials.item: grey-blue Welsh slate roof, steep pitch, a line of moss along the eaves
materials.why: Railway-era slate was the ordinary 1860s roof in Oxford villas

materials.item: front door of vertical oak boards under the horseshoe arch, dark-stained, black iron strap hinges and a plain iron latch, no knocker
materials.note: the Fish-Footman raps 'with his knuckles', so no knocker; boards and hinges inferred

details.item: broken crockery on the ground around the step: shards of white plates and a dented tin kettle lid, thrown out through the doorway
details.note: 'a large plate came skimming out... and broke to pieces against one of the trees'; ch006-p06 sound of 'a dish or kettle... broken to pieces'; also geography.json#LOC-duchess-house.visual_identifiers ('plates thrown out through the doorway')

details.item: a cast-iron boot-scraper set into the step and a bell-pull wire hanging beside the door with its handle missing
details.culture_ref: culture.json CUL-008 (doorstep service taken to the letter)
details.why: Period service-door furniture; the useless bell-pull echoes 'no sort of use in knocking'

details.item: the nearest tree trunk opposite the door is chipped pale where the plate shattered, shards at its foot
thin grey smoke leaking round the door frame and window edges
details.why: Links outside to the pepper-filled kitchen

details.item: a great letter on the step after the delivery, nearly as large as the Fish-Footman (prop owned by 06-art/prop)

scale_notes.rule: Two scales. (1) Arrival, ch005-p78, Alice at her usual height (135 cm): a 1:6 miniature of the same house, ridge about 1.2 m ('about four feet high'), placed in forced perspective in the clearing so the house comes up to Alice's chin. (2) After she nibbles down 'to nine inches high': the hero set is the full-size house (ridge 7.2 m, door 2.1 m) with the two footmen as CGI frog-bodied and fish-bodied figures in livery. Proposal (pending_H2, anatomy owned by 04-creatures/creature with 03-characters/appearance): both stand upright at about adult-servant height (about 1.6 m) so the 2.1 m door and step fit them as a real service door; Alice is staged in forced perspective at about the Frog-Footman's knee height (apparent 50 cm), a child among grown-up servants at the tradesmen's door; the text's nine inches is expressed by low camera and oversized door and step, not by literal ratio. The baby-to-pig exit (ch006-p45..p49) uses the same full-size hero set with Alice at her usual height (1:1, 135 cm), since she has played the kitchen at 1:1 (SCN-duchess-kitchen); the house then reads as an ordinary small house.
scale_notes.feeling: Shrinking herself before entering a stranger's house: politeness makes Alice small
scale_notes.why: The source gives only 'four feet high' and 'nine inches'; the two-build split keeps both beats shootable with the CGI footmen at a fixed servant scale (SUP-002 as amended BIB-0027)

negative: no thatched fairy-tale cottage, no Tudor half-timbering, no mushroom house
no grand manor, no porch columns, no lodge gates or estate walls
no door knocker, no house number, no nameplate
no plate glass, no gas or electric lamps outside; no clean bright new ornament (it is sooted)
no flowers or garden beds round the house; bare clearing only
no cartoon frog or fish faces, no humans in frog or fish costume; the footmen are CGI frog- and fish-bodied figures (anatomy pending_H2)
no flat poster illustration, outline graphics or matte-painting finish
prompt_ready_en: a small steep-gabled red brick house with dark blue brick bands in a sooted Art Nouveau style after Mucha, standing alone in a bare earthen clearing at the edge of a dense English wood, grey slate roof, a tall brick chimney pouring grey smoke, a horseshoe-arched door surround of carved stone lilies and vines around an oak plank door with black iron strap hinges above one worn stone step, a round stained-glass roundel in the gable and a cracked pastel-and-gold mosaic frieze under the eaves, small leaded windows smoked grey from inside, white plate shards scattered on the ground, photographed live-action set
